content.title: About
content.content: Whiting (also known as pangasius) is a mild‑flavored white fish commonly used in cooking. When fried, it develops a golden crust while keeping a tender, flaky texture and a characteristic sea taste. It is usually served hot as a standalone dish or as part of fast‑food meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whiting belongs to the carp family and is found in both freshwater and coastal waters worldwide.
Fried whiting is popular in Asian, European, and North American cuisines.
Proper frying retains most of the fish’s nutrients, including omega‑3 fatty acids.
The fish is often used in fish cakes, fish‑and‑chips, and as a filling for sushi rolls.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Whiting provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: The fish contains polyunsaturated fats that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Whiting supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It is a source of selenium, iodine, and phosphorus, which aid thyroid function and bone health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When fried moderately, whiting remains relatively low‑calorie compared with many other fried foods.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including whiting.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Depending on the source, the fish may contain traces of mercury or cadmium; choose reputable suppliers.

items.title: Over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive frying can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or sauces can raise sodium levels, which is a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fry whiting in vegetable oil until golden, serve with lemon, tartar sauce, or vegetable sides. It can be added to salads, sandwiches, or used as a sushi roll filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked fried whiting in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
